case_name: Shubham Parmar vs State Of Himachal Pradesh
facts_of_case: Complainant-victim X made a complaint under Section 156 (3) of Cr.P.C. seeking directions to SHO, Police Station Gagret for registration of FIR on 01.11.2019. The matter was investigated by the police leading to registration of FIR No.135 of 2019 against the bail petitioner. The case set up is that the complainant-victim and the bail petitioner were in talking terms since 2018, and consensually went to McLeodganj and stayed in Hotel Naddi Hills on 10.02.2019.

legal_principles.principle: The bail should be granted where the case is frivolous or groundless and no prima facie or reasonable grounds exist which lead to believe or point out towards accusation.
legal_principles.held: mandating that the bail (anticipatory or regular) is to be granted where the case is frivolous or groundless and no prima facie or reasonable grounds exists which lead to believe or point out towards accusation;
cited_cases: P. Chidambaram versus Directorate of Enforcement, (2019) 9 SCC 24
Sushila Aggarwal versus State-NCT Delhi, (2020) 5 SCC 01

legal_principles.principle: The nature of the crime has a huge relevance while considering the claim for bail.
legal_principles.held: in Para 25 that the nature of crime has a huge relevancy, while considering the claim for bail;
cited_cases: Deepak Yadav versus State of Uttar Pradesh, (2022) 8 SCC 559

legal_principles.principle: The order granting bail should reflect the judicial application of mind taking into consideration well-known parameters.
